findings.title: Water restores the stripped field
findings.claim: In the pericope, directed water meets land whose vegetation has been cut away, makes growth emerge, and turns the barren destination into a crop-bearing source. The water is shown as a routed restorative process, not as an isolated arrival.
findings.mechanism: The verb nasūqu gives the water a direction and destination; the barren-ground adjective supplies a state of lost vegetation; fa-nukhriju then makes crop emerge by means of that water. The sequence of water, land, crop and subsequent consumption also fits the preceding verse's surviving dwellings and ended human movement, setting historical loss beside material renewal.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the ecological sign as a connected process: water is directed, a stripped field becomes productive, and growth enters the life of the pericope.
findings.containment: The field begins as al-juruz, barren or stripped land. Fertility is the change made visible by water and crop; the finding does not claim that the land was already fertile, specify an irrigation system, or make the historical destruction in 32:26 identical to agricultural barrenness.

epistemic.reason: The focus surface supplies the water, destination, barren state, caused emergence and crop; trusted support ties them into one pericope-scale process. The unsupported water-appearance facet is explicitly excluded.

findings.title: Yield reaches animals and people
findings.claim: The field's renewal continues into nourishment: crop is not only brought forth but eaten by two named classes, the herd animals and the humans themselves, while the closing call to see can carry an inward-recognition resonance.
findings.mechanism: The focus names the crop, links eating back to it with minhu, coordinates anʿāmuhum and anfusuhum under the same eating verb, and closes with yubṣirūn. The previous verse's dwelling traces place this living distribution beside a past human landscape, while the focus's actual water makes a contextual life-sustaining-water branch available through the word for human selves.
findings.reader_payoff: The sign reaches past the field into bodies: animals and people both receive what the land produces, and seeing the process can become recognition of what sustains them.
findings.containment: The text names livestock and human selves as consumers, without specifying species, equal allotments, or a metaphysical account of the soul. The water branch under nafs is a contextual resonance from the explicit water-to-crop-to-eating chain; anfus itself is not translated as water.

epistemic.reason: The food distribution and paired perception are directly anchored. The benefit branch on livestock and the water branch under human selves are contextual, multi-step resonances, so the finding states their boundary and does not treat either as a plain lexical gloss.

findings.title: A corrective return meets a restored field
findings.claim: The preceding warning hopes that people will return after a nearer corrective experience; the focus shows water reaching stripped land and growth returning. Their relation lets ecological restoration carry an analogy of moral recoverability before the final outcome.
findings.mechanism: The 32:21 trace names tasting, nearness and hoped-for return. The focus trace assigns water delivery, barren terrain and renewed crop growth as the material field that meets those roles. The branch contacts change the focus from a self-contained natural restoration into an image that can also support a return while response remains possible.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold seriousness and recoverability together: a field depleted of growth is reached by water and becomes productive, just as the preceding verse makes return the hoped-for effect of a nearer corrective event.
findings.containment: This is an analogy between the human return named in 32:21 and the water-and-growth return in 32:27. It may remain a parallel rather than a repentance metaphor; the text does not state that agricultural restoration is a mechanism of forgiveness or that the two events are identical.

epistemic.reason: The exact Arabic anchors and trace coordinates support the contact, but reader_hft_a is legacy_unbound and its root/facet roles remain attributed nominations. The HFT itself preserves the live alternative that the water branch is only a resonance rather than a repentance metaphor.

findings.title: Historical traces are heard; renewal is seen
findings.claim: The previous verse places the traces of destroyed generations in surviving dwellings and closes by asking whether they hear or heed; the focus answers with a visible water-and-crop process framed by its own see and perceive questions. The focus becomes a second form of evidence alongside the historical one.
findings.mechanism: The HFT trace assigns guidance, destruction, movement, habitation and sign roles to 32:26, then assigns hearing/heeding to its closing appeal. These context carriers meet the focus's visible water, crop and repeated sight language, so the preceding historical trace and the present ecological process become complementary ways of encountering evidence.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees why the sequence moves from ruined habitations to a field in which water and growth can be watched: the prior sign is encountered through history and hearing, while this sign is encountered through ongoing material change and sight.
findings.containment: The paired media are a qualified reading: hearing in 32:26 can mean heeding, so the sensory contrast may be less sharp than the rhetorical pairing. The focus remains an agricultural sign in its own right; this does not rank hearing below sight or make the two forms mutually exclusive.

epistemic.reason: The exact 32:26 and 32:27 surfaces match the traced contacts, and the connection nomination supports the adjacent relation. The source reader is legacy_unbound and its word/root roles remain attributed; the live alternative is that hearing mainly means heeding.

branch_activations.carrier: The 32:26 word at HFT index 2, attributed the role of gentle guidance toward a path or truth.

findings.title: The field is an opening while response can still matter
findings.claim: The focus's water and crop form a present material opening, and its closing appeal to perceive can carry an opening of understanding, while the following verses ask about the final opening after which faith brings no benefit and no respite is given.
findings.mechanism: The focus gives water to barren land and brings crop out; 32:28 asks when the opening will come, and 32:29 names the day of opening while denying benefit and respite. The HFT trace brings the outlet-water and inward-release facets of fath back through the focus's water, crop-emergence and insight carriers.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the agricultural scene as more than evidence for a later event: it is a present supply and a present chance to perceive, set against a final opening when response has no further benefit.
findings.containment: The focus remains an agricultural event and 32:28–29 retain their final-opening reading. This is a contextual analogy of material supply and possible insight before that final moment; it does not identify irrigation with judgment or claim that the opening question names water.

epistemic.reason: The HFT supplies exact 32:28–29 Arabic, word indices, roles and a focus return, but reader_hft_a is legacy_unbound and context branches have no independent registry glosses. The agricultural opening may remain only a branch resonance, as the source itself notes.
